inclusion_criteria: Protein residues surrounding the ligand sufficiently resolved
Ligand is not simply solvent, ion, buffer, glycan, or crystallization additive
Structure retained regardless of whether GNINA or DiffDock later performs badly

explicit_exclusions.reason: Covalent inhibitor complex; not an apples-to-apples redocking test.
Quinazoline modulator covalently attached to Lys346; belongs in a separate covalent-docking benchmark.
N370S structure; listed small molecules are glycans/sulfate/glycerol, not a drug-like experimental ligand pose. Reserved for a future receptor-state robustness experiment.
Apo GCase at acidic pH; no ligand. Reserved for receptor-state experiments. Neutral-pH ligand-bound counterpart is 3GXF (included).

ligand_instance_selection_source: RCSB GraphQL API (data.rcsb.org/graphql), nonpolymer_entity_instances -> rcsb_nonpolymer_instance_validation_score (RSCC, RSR, average_occupancy, is_best_instance). Full raw query results are not committed (regenerable); the resolved per-case values are recorded below for audit.

amendments.reason: GCASE_VALIDATION_SET.md's frozen selection hierarchy (RSCC -> RSR -> occupancy -> B-factor -> chain id) only covers multiple instances of the SAME ligand of interest, not two different LOI compounds bound simultaneously. Extended the same underlying principle ('best experimental ligand-quality evidence') to this case: A1IBG's best instance has RSCC 0.935 / RSR 0.103 / occupancy 0.76, materially better than A1IBE's best instance (RSCC 0.819 / RSR 0.228 / occupancy 0.53). amendments.change: 3GXF: selected the RCSB-flagged is_best_instance ligand copy (chain D, resseq 512) over chain B/resseq 517, despite the latter having marginally higher RSCC (0.995 vs 0.994) and marginally lower RSR (0.026 vs 0.031).

amendments.change: Switched reference_ligands/ from legacy PDB to SDF (heavy atoms only, bonds/orders assigned via RCSB chem-comp SMILES template, coordinates from the deposited experimental structure).
amendments.reason: CRITICAL BUG, caught before any docking ran: the initial extraction wrote reference ligands as legacy PDB via Bio.PDB's PDBIO. Legacy PDB's residue-name field is only 3 characters wide; the nine 9F* ligand component IDs (e.g. A1IBD) are 5 characters, so PDBIO silently wrote them anyway, shifting every downstream fixed-width column -- including X/Y/Z coordinates -- by 2 characters. Any fixed-column reader (BioPython's own PDBParser, and any docking tool reading PDB by column position, not just whitespace-split) would silently misparse coordinates. Verified directly: reading the standard PDB column offsets (30:38, 38:46, 46:54) off an affected line returned garbled, unusable numbers. This is also why RCSB has no legacy-PDB download for these entries at all (confirmed: 404) -- the format cannot represent them. Fixed by re-parsing from the (unaffected) mmCIF source, perceiving heavy-atom connectivity from 3D geometry (rdDetermineBonds.DetermineConnectivity), assigning correct bond orders via AllChem.AssignBondOrdersFromTemplate against each ligand's RCSB canonical SMILES, and writing SDF (no fixed-column format limitation). Receptor files were never affected (protein residue codes are always <=3 characters). All 14 SDFs round-trip through RDKit cleanly; 9FA6's independently-perceived 3D chirality came out R, cross-confirming both the RCSB SMILES stereo descriptor and the earlier enantiomer decision. Hydrogens are intentionally dropped from the reference ligand files (heavy-atom RMSD is the field-standard practice -- GNINA/DiffDock poses are heavy-atom only too).

amendments.change: Rebuilt reference_ligands/*.sdf bond-order assignment to use each case's docking_input_protonated_smiles (pH 7.4, dimorphite-dl) as the AssignBondOrdersFromTemplate template, instead of the plain neutral RCSB canonical SMILES used at first extraction. Heavy-atom 3D coordinates are untouched (verified: max coordinate delta 0.0 across all 14 cases before/after) -- only the formal-charge/bond-order labels on the same atoms changed.
amendments.reason: BUG, found while scoring the first real GNINA/DiffDock-L results (not before -- see made_before_seeing_docking_results below): decisionbench_dd_docking.rmsd.symmetry_aware_rmsd (rdMolAlign.CalcRMS) does substructure-match-based atom correspondence, which by default requires matching formal charges atom-for-atom. The original reference ligands were built neutral, but every docking pose reflects the protonated SMILES actually fed to the tools (docking_input_ligands/, docking_input_protonated_smiles) -- net charges of +1/+2/-1 depending on the case. That charge mismatch made CalcRMS raise 'No sub-structure match found' for 10 of 14 cases outright, not a chemistry problem, a representation inconsistency between two stages of this project's own pipeline.
amendments.why_this_does_not_violate_the_no_post_ho: This is not a qualification threshold, scoring formula, or gate -- it's a mechanical bond-order/charge-labeling fix applied identically and structurally to all 14 cases and both tools, required just to get RMSD to compute at all (the pipeline crashed before producing any Success@1/@5 numbers, so there was no favorable-vs-unfavorable result to react to). Heavy-atom coordinates, which are what RMSD actually measures, are provably unchanged.
amendments.audit_report: reference_ligand_reprotonation_report.json (old/new net charge and max coordinate delta per case)

amendments.change: Fixed the ligand-protonation variant-selection rule to exclude a PROTONATED sulfonamide nitrogen ([NH+] attached to S(=O)(=O)), not just a deprotonated one ([N-]), before counting 'good ammonium' sites. Corrected 3 of 14 cases -- 9FAY, 9FAZ, 9FB2 -- from net charge +2 to the chemically correct +1. Re-embedded docking_input_ligands/*.sdf for those 3 and re-synced reference_ligands/*.sdf's bond-order template to match (coordinate delta 0.0, same pattern as the prior amendment). The other 11 cases were unaffected (re-ran the full 14-case selection to confirm: only these 3 changed).
amendments.reason: External review caught this: a sulfonamide nitrogen, even N,N-disubstituted, is far too weak a base (electron-withdrawing sulfonyl group) to be protonated at pH 7.4 -- a genuine aliphatic amine (pKaH ~9-10) is the correct protonation site. The original selection rule's GOOD_AMMONIUM SMARTS ([NH3+,NH2+,NH+]) matched a protonated sulfonamide N just as readily as a real amine, and its 'maximize ammonium count' tie-break rewarded the spurious double-protonation over the chemically correct single-protonation variant that dimorphite-dl had also proposed.
amendments.why_this_does_not_violate_the_no_post_ho: Not a qualification threshold or scoring change -- a chemistry correctness fix to the protonation-state assignment, caught by review before any RMSD result was produced FOR THESE 3 CASES specifically (GNINA/DiffDock had already run once on the old, wrong protonation state, but that prior run's Success@1/@5 numbers for these 3 cases are being discarded, not selectively kept or compared against).
amendments.requires_rerun_note: Docking INPUT changed (different net charge -> different 3D-embedded starting conformer) for these 3 cases. GNINA and DiffDock-L must be re-run on the GPU instance for exactly these 3 PDB IDs; the other 11 cases' existing docking_runs/ output remains valid and does not need to be re-run.

file_layout.raw_pdb/<PDB_ID>.cif: Full mmCIF structure as downloaded from RCSB (files.rcsb.org). Legacy .pdb format is unavailable for the 9F* entries because their 5-character ligand component IDs (e.g. A1IBE) do not fit the legacy PDB format's 3-character residue-name field.
file_layout.receptors/<PDB_ID>_receptor_raw.pdb: All standard polymer (protein) residues only -- waters, ions, glycans, and every heteroatom (including the reference ligand itself) removed. Only the primary altloc/blank-altloc atoms kept. Not yet protonated.
file_layout.receptors_prepared/<PDB_ID>_prepared.pdb: Protonated at pH 7.4 via PDB2PQR 3.7.1 (AMBER force field, PROPKA titration), missing side-chain atoms rebuilt, output as PDB. See redocking_protocol_v1.0.json for the frozen parameters and per-structure warnings (backbone gaps, alternate occupancies) logged during preparation.
file_layout.reference_ligands/<PDB_ID>_<COMP_ID>.sdf: The single selected ligand-of-interest instance, HEAVY ATOMS ONLY, with bond orders assigned from the RCSB canonical SMILES template and 3D coordinates from the deposited experimental structure at the alt_id_selected conformer. See the 2026-08-22 amendment above for why this is SDF, not PDB.
file_layout.extraction_report_ligands.json: Per-case audit: heavy-atom count, template bond-order assignment success, and formula cross-check against the RCSB chem-comp record.
